stem: Young leaves show interveinal chlorosis even though iron is present in the feed solution and root-zone pH has drifted high. What is the strongest interpretation?
choices: Iron may be present but poorly available in the current root-zone chemistry
Iron can never affect young tissue
More total EC always fixes the problem
Root-zone pH is unrelated to micronutrient availability
rationale: Micronutrient supply in the reservoir does not guarantee availability at the root; pH can strongly influence several micronutrients.
